arguments.sql_query:
SELECT MAX(condition_start_date) AS max_condition_date, MIN(condition_start_date) AS min_condition_date
FROM omop.condition_occurrence

WITH lung_concepts AS (
  SELECT descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor
  WHERE ancestor_concept_id = 258369 -- Primary malignant neoplasm of lung
  UNION SELECT 258369
  UNION SELECT descendant_concept_id FROM omop.concept_ancestor WHERE ancestor_concept_id = 443388 -- Malignant neoplasm of lung
  UNION SELECT 443388
), first_lung_dx AS (
  SELECT co.person_id, MIN(co.condition_start_date) AS first_dx_date
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN lung_concepts lc ON co.condition_concept_id = lc.concept_id
  WHERE co.condition_start_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY co.person_id
), bounds AS (
  SELECT MAX(first_dx_date) AS max_dx_date FROM first_lung_dx
)
SELECT max_dx_date, DATEADD(year, -3, max_dx_date) AS window_start, COUNT(*) AS incident_patients_in_all_time
FROM first_lung_dx CROSS JOIN bounds
GROUP BY max_dx_date

WITH lung_concepts AS (
  SELECT descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor
  WHERE ancestor_concept_id IN (258369, 443388) -- primary malignant neoplasm of lung; malignant neoplasm of lung
  UNION SELECT 258369
  UNION SELECT 443388
), first_lung_dx AS (
  SELECT co.person_id, MIN(co.condition_start_date) AS first_dx_date
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN lung_concepts lc ON co.condition_concept_id = lc.concept_id
  WHERE co.condition_start_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY co.person_id
), bounds AS (
  SELECT MAX(first_dx_date) AS max_dx_date FROM first_lung_dx
), monthly AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(first_dx_date), MONTH(first_dx_date), 1) AS date) AS diagnosis_month,
    COUNT(*) AS incident_diagnoses
  FROM first_lung_dx
  CROSS JOIN bounds
  WHERE first_dx_date >= DATEADD(year, -3, max_dx_date)
    AND first_dx_date <= max_dx_date
  GROUP BY DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(first_dx_date), MONTH(first_dx_date), 1)
)
SELECT diagnosis_month, incident_diagnoses
FROM monthly
ORDER BY diagnosis_month

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT diagnosis_month, COUNT(*) AS incident_diagnoses
FROM (
  SELECT person_id, CAST(DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(MIN(condition_start_date)), MONTH(MIN(condition_start_date)), 1) AS date) AS diagnosis_month, MIN(condition_start_date) AS first_dx_date
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence
  WHERE condition_concept_id IN (
    SELECT descendant_concept_id FROM omop.concept_ancestor WHERE ancestor_concept_id IN (258369, 443388)
    UNION SELECT 258369
    UNION SELECT 443388
  )
    AND condition_start_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY person_id
) first_lung_dx
WHERE first_dx_date >= DATEADD(year, -3, (SELECT MAX(first_dx_date) FROM (
  SELECT person_id, MIN(condition_start_date) AS first_dx_date
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence
  WHERE condition_concept_id IN (
    SELECT descendant_concept_id FROM omop.concept_ancestor WHERE ancestor_concept_id IN (258369, 443388)
    UNION SELECT 258369
    UNION SELECT 443388
  )
    AND condition_start_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY person_id
) all_first_dx))
GROUP BY diagnosis_month
ORDER BY diagnosis_month

content.text:
Monthly incident lung-cancer diagnoses were **fairly stable in 2023–2024**, then show a **sharp decline in mid-to-late 2025**, which is likely influenced by incomplete/censored recent data.

- **Case definition:** first recorded lung-cancer diagnosis per patient, using OMOP descendants of lung malignant neoplasm concepts.
- **Window:** 2022-12 to 2025-12, anchored to latest observed incident lung-cancer date: **2025-12-05**.
- **2023:** 1,251 incident diagnoses; mean **104/month**.
- **2024:** 1,228 incident diagnoses; mean **102/month** — essentially flat vs 2023.
- **2025:** 716 incident diagnoses; mean **60/month**, but the drop is concentrated after May:
  - Jan–May 2025: ~**96/month**
  - Jun–Dec 2025: ~**34/month**

Notable peaks were **Mar 2023: 124**, **May 2024: 120**, and **Jan 2025: 116**. The apparent decline after mid-2025 should be interpreted cautiously as likely reflecting data-lag or incomplete capture rather than a true epidemiologic decrease.
